clue.text: Rigged poll, one with climb for Trump, say

indicators.note: a rigged vote has been fiddled with, so the letters before it are tampered with and rearranged

blocks.note: the three words taken as letters to be rearranged; 'with' just joins them

explanation.surface: A fixed election in which someone made a bid for the top, the way Trump did.
explanation.walkthrough: COLONEL BLIMP is a British cartoon character from the 1930s, a pompous, blustering reactionary whose name became a byword for that type.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter offers a loud, bombastic right-wing figure as a modern example of the blustering reactionary the cartoon character embodies.

clue.text: The devil is here!

blocks.note: second meaning: in this world, among the living

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation reads like an alarm that Satan has arrived; instead both halves are phrases that slot into the same idioms.
explanation.definitionFit: 'What the devil?' and 'what on earth?' are interchangeable intensifiers, and life in this world is life on earth.

clue.text: They can make people cry about religious beliefs

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the vegetables wrap round the short word for religious

blocks.note: chopping these vegetables brings tears to the eyes
PI is short for pious, a crossword standard for religious

explanation.surface: Views on faith can move people to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: The short word for religious sits after the first letter of the tear-jerking vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinions are the views a person holds, which is a straightforward synonym for beliefs.

clue.text: Border collie pulled dog sledge finally

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of each of the four words before it

blocks.note: the final letters of the four words in turn

explanation.surface: A Border collie hauling a sled at the end of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border collie' looks like a fixed breed name, but Border is detached to serve as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A border is the outer rim or margin of something, the same as its edge.

clue.text: One who swears bars help me to get drunk

indicators.note: drunk words stagger about, so the letters before it lose their order

explanation.surface: A foul-mouthed drinker pleads with the pubs to help him get drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who utters profanities against the sacred is literally a person using bad language, so swearing fits.

clue.text: I laugh, having got American lawyer in a state

indicators.note: having got something in means taking it inside, so the first part encloses the lawyer

blocks.note: a DA is a district attorney, a US prosecutor
a laughing sound, as in ho ho

explanation.surface: Someone laughs off getting a lawyer while they are in a bit of a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' reads as being flustered, but 'in' only links and the state is a US one.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty United States, in the north-west of the country.

clue.text: Advocate of premier with power going to head

indicators.note: going to head means placed at the front, so the power symbol leads

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
a premier is a head of government

explanation.surface: A supporter of a prime minister who has grown too powerful.
explanation.definitionFit: An advocate pleads a case in court, so a person who argues on someone's behalf is a pleader.

clue.text: Denial made by conservative in Tory convention

indicators.note: in tells us the single letter goes inside the following words

blocks.note: CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party

explanation.surface: A rebuttal delivered by a right-winger at the party conference.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory convention looks like a party conference; it splits into the party name and a synonym for custom.
explanation.definitionFit: A contradiction asserts the opposite of a statement, so it is a flat rejection or gainsaying of it.

clue.text: Heartier apple crumbles for a painterly type

indicators.note: something that crumbles breaks into pieces, so the letters fall apart and regroup

explanation.surface: A more substantial apple crumble is served to an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple crumbles' reads as a pudding; crumbles is the verb that breaks up the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood were Victorian painters, so a member or follower is an artistic sort of person.

clue.text: Jumbo pen in German stores or The Gap?

indicators.note: stores means keeps inside, so the run of words before it holds the answer within them

blocks.note: the letters run from the tail of the first word to the head of the last

explanation.surface: A shopper hunts for an outsize pen in German shops, or perhaps in the clothing chain Gap.
explanation.walkthrough: Gap is an American clothing chain, which is why shops fill the surface, but stores is the verb doing the hiding and The Gap is simply a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening is a space or breach in something, which is exactly what a gap is.

clue.text: You punching a GM, perhaps, is unprofessional

indicators.note: punching means thrusting into something, so the word for you goes inside

blocks.note: a chess grandmaster delivers checkmate, so is a mater

explanation.surface: Throwing a punch at a general manager is no way to behave at work.
explanation.walkthrough: GM looks like a general manager; in chess it is a grandmaster, someone who mates opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur does something for love rather than pay, so the word works as an adjective for non-professional.

clue.text: Structural supports built into altar sides

indicators.note: built into says the letters are embedded within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Load-bearing parts constructed into the sides of a church altar.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsi are bones of the ankle and plates stiffening the eyelids, both framework that holds the body up.

clue.text: Excited by hot senior in Wonderbra, possibly

blocks.note: H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A man aroused by an attractive older woman in a push-up bra.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wonderbra is a brand of push-up brassiere, an example of something that props up and supports.

clue.text: Yellow type that might give you the slip?

definitions.text: Yellow type that might give you the slip?

blocks.clueFragment: Yellow type that might give you the slip?
blocks.note: surface reading: a cowardly sort who might run off and evade you

blocks.clueFragment: Yellow type that might give you the slip?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a yellow piece of fruit skin that might make you slip and fall

explanation.walkthrough: Yellow means cowardly and giving someone the slip means escaping them; literally, the yellow item is the classic comedy pratfall prop.
explanation.definitionFit: The discarded skin of the yellow fruit is the cartoon cause of slipping over.

clue.text: Front of aluminium fences had turned very pale

indicators.note: front of picks out only the first letter of the metal named
turned means twisted round, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The front of metal fencing had gone a ghostly colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ashen-faced has gone grey with shock or illness, the colour of ash, so drained of colour.

clue.text: ‘Take LSD’ is helpful advice, Republican admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let inside, so the party letter goes in

explanation.surface: A Republican is caught recommending acid as a useful pointer.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip is slang for experiencing a hallucinogenic drug, so the verb means taking acid.

clue.text: Heroin-packed opiate I shot being a state

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are broken and rearranged
packed means stuffed with, so the drug letter is placed inside

explanation.surface: A drug user injected opiates and ended up in a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being a state' suggests being out of it; the state is a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethiopia is a sovereign country in the Horn of Africa, and a nation is a state.

clue.text: Lazy person people greatly admire on radio

indicators.note: on radio means heard rather than seen, so we go by the sound of the word

explanation.surface: A lazy radio celebrity whom the public adores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lazy person' looks like the definition, but person belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle describes someone not working or unwilling to make an effort, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Singer with Queen and soprano can be mischief-makers

explanation.surface: A singer joining Queen and a soprano might cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Singer suggests a human vocalist; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkers are people who lark about, playing pranks and fooling around, so they cause mischief.

clue.text: Wild beasts near wet patch of earth

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Untamed animals close to a soggy bit of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet patch of earth' reads as boggy ground; it is a body of water on the planet Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barents Sea is part of the Arctic Ocean off northern Norway and Russia, a watery area of the globe.

clue.text: Cook will have way with a flight attendant

blocks.note: RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A chef has his way with an air hostess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a' places A next to the road abbreviation, and it comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward serves passengers on an aircraft or ship, the role of cabin crew.

clue.text: Renegade performer with company a pest ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a turn is a variety act or performer

explanation.surface: A disloyal actor whose troupe found him a nuisance in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: In British variety theatre a turn is an individual act on the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat switches sides, abandoning a cause, which is what a renegade does.

clue.text: Tea ceremony in African country close to Morocco

indicators.note: close to means the end, so only the last letter of the place is taken

blocks.note: a landlocked nation in north-central Africa

explanation.surface: A tea ritual held in an African nation near Morocco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to Morocco' reads as geographically near; it means the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chado, literally the way of tea, is the Japanese name for the formal tea-making ritual.

clue.text: Slormgorm had ecstasy together with a large model

blocks.note: the setter is I, so the setter had is I'd
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
L for large, a clothing size

explanation.surface: The setter took a pill along with a big catwalk star.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often name themselves to stand for I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect example to be copied, the sense in which a model is a pattern to follow.

clue.text: Stop making primarily terrific love to get ring

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the next word is used
making one letter into another means swapping it out for the replacement

blocks.note: O is zero, love in tennis

explanation.surface: Stop turning great lovemaking into a commitment with a wedding ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The T at the end of the word for stop changes into the tennis score for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is a circle of light around the head of a saint, so it is a luminous circle.

clue.text: Old judge getting to grips with training in work

indicators.note: getting to grips with means clasping something, so the surrounding words hold the training

explanation.surface: An elderly magistrate tackles a workplace course.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to function or run, the sense in which a machine is said to work.

clue.text: One by the kerbside idiot with vice picked up

indicators.note: picked up means caught by the ear, so it is the sound that counts

blocks.note: an ass is a fool and a fault is a failing

explanation.surface: A fool with a bad habit is arrested on the pavement.
explanation.walkthrough: Picked up suggests an arrest; it means heard. The kerb is the edge of a pavement, and the road surface runs right beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is the tarry road surfacing that lies alongside the kerb, so it is one thing found there.

clue.text: After swimming about, do prawns lose ounces?

indicators.note: swimming about means moving here and there, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A dieting question: do prawns shed weight after a swim?
explanation.walkthrough: Ounces looks like a weight; an ounce is also another name for the big cat of the Himalayas.
explanation.definitionFit: Ounce is the old alternative name for the snow leopard, a usage much loved by crossword setters.
